item.title: How hotter weather is making us poorer
item.description:
The last 11 years have been the planet’s hottest on record. This changing climate is manifested in extreme weather events like heat waves and wildfires. But less obvious are the higher prices and lower wages linked to a heating world.
According to a 2026 study by the MIT Sloan School of Management and Ucla School of Law, climate change has already driven up average American household expenses by $900 a year — rising to above $1,300 for one in 10 US counties.
These costs would not exist in a world without climate change. They include escalating home insurance ($600 higher on average), increasing state and federal taxes due to disaster recovery costs or health impacts from wildfire smoke, for example.
“Climate inaction isn’t just an environmental failure; it acts like a tax on every American household,” wrote the researchers.
A 2024 report by Germany’s Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact estimated that climate damages to agriculture, infrastructure, health and productivity could cost the world economy $38 trillion a year by 2050.
But how have climate-driven weather extremes already impacted salaries and household budgets?
“If we can’t figure out what climate change is already costing us with the data we have, projecting the future becomes almost hopeless,” said Derek Lemoine, an economics professor from the University of Arizona who has estimated a 12% reduction in US incomes as global temperatures have risen. This is also compared to a non-climate change scenario.
Lemoine shows how temperature extremes in one US county are having cascading economic impacts in distant locations with milder weather due to interconnected trade and supply chains.
“Much work studies climate change as if it changes weather in only one year and one location at a time,” Lemoine told DW.
Instead, he wants to understand how, if a heat wave wipes out corn crops across America, other industries that rely on that corn, including livestock and food producers, will be impacted as the commodity becomes scarcer and increases in price.
“As your costs have gone up,” said Lemoine of producers impacted across the corn supply chain, “that’s going to serve to make the income of everyone who depends on you go down.”
Climate’s impact on trade is also being felt in Germany, where record low water levels on the Rhine River, the busiest inland trade waterway in Europe, could shave as much as 0.2% off Germany’s economic output in the third quarter of 2026, noted the Kiel Institute for the World Economy in July.
Prolonged dry weather linked to climate change is to blame as shipping capacity drops to as low as 15% on the river that connects Europe’s largest port in Rotterdam in the Netherlands with much of western Germany.
One Australian study also looks at how broad climate changes, rather than local shocks from single extreme weather events, have gradually led to a decrease in productivity and economic output.
Timothy Neal, a researcher at the Institute for Climate Risk and Response at the University of New South Wales in Australia, co-authored the report showing that global heating reduced economic output in the state of NSW by an average of around 18%, or the equivalent of $21,288 Australian dollars per person in 2024.
“The damage has already been quite severe,” Neal told DW, adding that in a non-warming scenario, citizens would enjoy “lower food prices” and “lower poverty.”
The report refers to droughts in parts of NSW in the mid-late 2010s that reduced productivity across the whole state by up to 10 billion Australian dollars due to lower agricultural yields and farm incomes, higher water costs and increased reliance on government assistance.
These financial impacts compounded through the state economy over time, influencing the cost of food, insurance and infrastructure maintenance.
In the words of the report, these effects also “compound existing economic pressures and contribute to widening disparities between regions,” meaning an increase in income and wealth inequality.
“Climate change action should not be seen as a predominantly environmental but also economically sensible,” said Frank Jotzo, an economist at the NSW Net Zero Commission, which works to decarbonize the state and commissioned the above study.
Referring to “defensive climate investments” such as reinforcing roads, railways and shipping infrastructure to adapt to a hotter world, Jotzo added that “if it wasn’t for climate change, we could be putting that money and that effort into other things.”
However, adaptation efforts such as the greening of cities to reduce heat island effects will be vital in order to head off much worse future economic impacts.
The 2026 European heat waves, for example, have already cost around €180 billion, which is the EU’s entire projected economic growth for the year, according to one analysis.
Adaptation will also involve strengthening the hospital and medical system to counteract the health effects of heat waves that also reduce productivity as heat-stressed employees tire or struggle to sleep, Jotzo noted.
But Lemoine says that adaptation to climate-driven economic decline is so “costly in its own right” that it could exacerbate income loss and be ineffective if not done comprehensively.
Only when “all places” are insulated from weather extremes, can the cascading economic impacts be addressed, he says.
Nonetheless, both adaptation and a rapid reduction of planet-heating emissions are together required to avoid climate-driven income loss that will worsen if warming outstrips Paris climate agreement targets.
“Unchecked climate change would create a permanent drain on wages and productivity,” said Jotzo.

item.title: Salahuddin urges crime reporters to play responsible role in building safer society
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Wednesday urged crime reporters to play a responsible and objective role in preventing crime and building a safer society, saying their role is becoming increasingly important as the nature of crime changes with advances in technology.
He came up with the call while speaking as the chief guest at a program marking the 43rd founding anniversary of the Bangladesh Crime Reporters Association (CRAB) at Segunbagicha in the capital.
The minister said the government will consider providing assistance, either through government initiatives or corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds, to crime reporters who are injured or otherwise affected while performing their professional duties.
He also said the government will examine, subject to legal considerations, whether certificates could be awarded by the Ministry of Home Affairs or the police department to recognize professional excellence and investigative journalism.
Salahuddin said crime reporting is different from many other journalistic beats and is largely a form of investigative journalism that involves risks.
As the nature of crime changes, journalists also need to improve their knowledge of technology and emerging forms of crime, he said.
The minister said crime reporters have a significant role in building a crime-free and secure society, while stressing that responsible and objective journalism is essential alongside modern legal frameworks to prevent and combat technology-driven crimes.
He said the media, police and the Ministry of Home Affairs are interconnected in combating crime and maintaining law and order, and that an organization like CRAB has an important role in providing information and suggestions in this regard.
Salahuddin said CRAB, with 318 professional members, has established a respected position in investigative journalism over its 43-year journey.
He described investigative journalism as a knowledge-based field requiring extensive study and analysis of information.
Emphasising the need to identify the underlying causes of crime, the minister said crime should not be treated merely as a symptom and that its underlying causes must be addressed.
He identified drugs and gambling as major driving forces behind many serious crimes and said society must be analysed to understand why crimes occur, rather than focusing solely on punishing offenders.
Salahuddin said the government has taken steps to update the legal framework to address emerging crimes, including online gambling and drug-related offences.
Referring to the decline in acid-related crimes, he said strong laws, media attention and social awareness have contributed to reducing such offences and called for similar joint efforts to tackle drugs, online gambling and other crimes.
Describing the media as a mirror of society, the minister said journalists' active and responsible participation, alongside the government and law enforcement agencies, is essential to reducing crime.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,044 as eight die in 24 hours
item.description:
Eight more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Wednesday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,044 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all eight latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 944, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 100.
A total of 1,239 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to175,198.
Meanwhile, 81 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 20,282.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 154,420 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 148,465 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Bangladeshi dies after falling from stairs amid ‘missile alert’ in Jeddah
item.description:
A 25-year-old Bangladeshi man died reportedly after suffering a head injury while rushing down stairs amid a missile alert in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, early Tuesday.
The deceased was identified as Saurav Islam, son of Amir Islam of Musapur village under Raipura upazila in Narsingdi.
According to his family members, Saurav was on the rooftop of the house where he lived in Jeddah.
Panic gripped him after seeing a missile reportedly approaching the city from Yemen on his mobile phone, and he hurriedly tried to come down the stairs.
At one stage, a rope reportedly got entangled around one of his feet, causing him to fall and suffer a severe head injury. He bled profusely.
His co-workers later found him lying in a pool of blood after waking up in the morning.
Local police recovered the body, and legal proceedings are underway, Bangladeshi expatriates said.
Saurav had been working as a tea boy at a bank in Jeddah for about five years, according to his relatives.
The family came to know about his death in the afternoon when one of his co-workers in Saudi Arabia contacted them over the phone.
Saurav was the only son of his parents. His mother, Renu Begum, has reportedly been fainting since learning of his death.
The parents said they want to see their son one last time and bury him with their own hands. They appealed to the government to take steps to bring Saurav’s body back to Bangladesh as soon as possible.
The sudden death has cast a pall of grief over the village.
Raipura Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Masud Rana said he heard about the incident, but no one has contacted the administration yet. “If they contact us, necessary assistance will be provided,” he said.

item.title: 180-day review finds gaps in govt action on women, children’s rights
item.description:
A review of the government’s first 180 days has found gaps in implementing its election manifesto commitments on women’s and children’s rights, with speakers calling for stronger political commitment, clearer implementation plans and regular accountability.
The review identified shortcomings in implementation planning, prevention of child marriage and child labor, health financing, inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection of marginalized groups and regular accountability.
At the same time, progress was noted in areas including budget allocations, school feeding, health service initiatives, expansion of one-stop crisis centers and disability allowance measures.
The findings were presented at a discussion titled “From Commitment to Implementation: The Government’s 180 Days in Protecting the Rights of Women and Children,” organized by the Coalition for Advancing Equality and Justice at Hotel Lakeshore in Gulshan on Wednesday.
The review covered five areas: education; health and nutrition; protection from violence; climate risk and WASH; and diversity and inclusion.
Presenting the keynote, Wasiur Rahman Tonmoy, Lead for Youth and Social Cohesion at Manusher Jonno Foundation, and Rowshon Akhter Urmee, Gender Justice and Social Inclusion Specialist at Oxfam in Bangladesh, outlined the progress and gaps identified in the review.
They recommended faster action on an anti-discrimination law, stronger measures to prevent child marriage and child labor, curriculum reform, health insurance, inclusive WASH systems, manifesto-based budgeting and regular reviews of progress.
Opening the discussion on behalf of the coalition, Kabita Bose, Country Director of Plan International Bangladesh, said the coalition was formed by seven national and international organizations ahead of the 13th National Parliamentary Election to bring women’s and children’s rights more prominently into political and development discussions.
The coalition had submitted evidence-based recommendations to 14 political parties, she said, noting that women, children, girls and young people often receive less priority in election manifestos.
“Investment in women and children should not be seen as charity, but as a rights-based and strategic development priority,” Bose said.
She said the coalition wanted to work with the government and other stakeholders to review progress, identify gaps and support implementation of the commitments.
Political representation
During the panel discussion, BNP reserved-seat MP Anna Minj said women elected through reserved seats were active and capable, but their direct political representation remained constrained by party structures, nomination barriers, election costs and online harassment.
She said the 33% target for women’s participation had not yet been fully implemented and argued that meaningful inclusion should begin within political parties through greater representation of women and other marginalized groups.
Dr Nazneen Ahmed, Executive Director of the Centre for Policy Dialogue, identified financial capacity, priority setting and governance as key challenges.
“Women need equity, not just equality, because years of policy gaps have kept them behind,” she said.
Nazneen also called for initiatives such as the Pink Bus service to be reviewed after several months to determine whether they were reducing harassment or creating new barriers for women.
Dr Md Shafiqul Islam Masud, Jamaat-e-Islami MP from Patuakhali-2, said women’s and children’s rights required political unity, safe workplaces, improved healthcare, childcare support and faster access to justice.
Many incidents of violence may remain unreported because victims fear retaliation or cannot afford legal action, he said, calling on political parties to take a zero-tolerance position on violence against women and children.
Nusrat Tabassum Jyoti, a reserved-seat MP from the National Citizens Party, said women and children continued to face insecurity at home, in public spaces, online and while seeking justice.
She stressed the need to ensure nutritious food for women and girls from childhood and called for stronger protection against violence, clearer safeguards in cyber laws and measures to address deepfake-based abuse.
Climate vulnerability
Md Shamsuddoha, Chief Executive of the Centre for Participatory Research and Development, said climate change was affecting women and children beyond the immediate impacts of cyclones, river erosion and heatwaves.
He pointed to waterlogging, crop losses, migration, child labor, school dropout and poverty as interconnected consequences of climate vulnerability.
He called for human-centered climate planning, stronger governance of climate finance and greater integration of climate action into national development planning.
Govt response
Speaking as chief guest, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj thanked the coalition for reviewing manifesto commitments and maintaining public scrutiny of political pledges.
He said democratic politics should be based on merit, public service and people’s trust rather than muscle power.
“We must stop dividing ourselves and work together to build a society where women are recognized not only by family roles of being someone’s daughter, mother or wife, but by their own identity and contribution,” Hajjaj said.
He also said temporary measures such as reserved parliamentary seats and Pink Bus services might remain necessary until equal rights and opportunities were ensured.
However, the ultimate goal should be a society where women could participate safely, directly and with dignity, he said.
Hajjaj said the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education was working to strengthen monitoring of primary schools, madrasas and other educational institutions.
The ministry was also planning to pilot free sanitary supplies and awareness programs for adolescent girls and support education infrastructure in haor and other remote areas, he added.
Anil Pant, Country Director of Oxfam in Bangladesh, delivered the vote of thanks.
The Coalition for Advancing Equality and Justice comprises Breaking the Silence, JAAGO Foundation, Manusher Jonno Foundation, Oxfam in Bangladesh, Plan International Bangladesh, Save the Children in Bangladesh and WaterAid Bangladesh.

item.title: Gaza apartment block collapse leaves 20 dead, many missing
item.description:
Gaza authorities said Wednesday that at least 20 people including five children had died and dozens more were missing after an apartment building collapsed from damage sustained in earlier Israeli strikes.
The six-story building, which had four apartments per floor, crumbled overnight onto nearby homes and tents in the Tal al-Hawa area of Gaza City, according to the civil defense agency, which works as a rescue service under Hamas authority.
The vast majority of buildings in Gaza have been damaged or destroyed in Israeli strikes throughout the war with Hamas, according to the United Nations.
AFP journalists saw the collapsed building reduced to an immense pile of shattered concrete, towering over a team of rescuers in high-visibility vests conducting a desperate search.
Excavators bearing Egyptian flags worked to remove the debris next to rows of tents for displaced people, while rescuers and volunteers carried out the dead wrapped in white plastic body bags.
“My friend and neighbors live in this building. I came to help my friend retrieve some clothes and mattresses. He currently has no shelter or home,” Mohannad Al-Mashharawi told AFP.
Civil defense agency spokesman Mahmoud Basal told AFP the building had sustained structural damage from previous Israeli strikes.
The bodies of “20 martyrs have been recovered from the rubble,” he said.
“Among the dead are five infants, while dozens of people remain trapped beneath the debris,” he added.
He said rescue operations were ongoing but relied on “limited equipment and basic tools, as the Israeli occupation prevents the entry of necessary heavy machinery and equipment into the Gaza Strip.”
The building was hit multiple times in 2024 and March 2025, leading to warnings for Gazans not to go back, Basal said.
“They have no other choice. With neither tents nor homes available, they are living in cracked, damaged buildings despite the risk of collapse,” he added.
The ensuing Israeli military campaign has killed more than 73,700 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
With so many Palestinians left homeless, and major shortages of construction materials, many Gaza residents have taken the risk of moving into the shaky buildings.
The UN’s humanitarian coordinator for the occupied Palestinian territories, Ramiz Alakbarov, said he was “devastated” by Wednesday’s reports of the building collapse.
“Today’s tragedy underscores the grave risks faced by families living in these structures and the urgent need for safer alternatives. No one should have to risk their life simply to find a safe place to shelter,” he said in a statement.
Gaza’s civil defense agency has identified around 2,000 buildings in the territory that it says are at risk of collapse.
The Gaza government media office under Hamas pointed to delays in reconstruction of the enclave.
“We hold the Israeli occupation and the international community fully and directly responsible for this catastrophe befalling our Palestinian people,” it said.
Israel has allowed additional aid into Gaza since the declaration of a US-brokered ceasefire in October 2025.
But Israel has kept carrying out strikes and has restricted the entry of a range of equipment that it says could also have military use.

item.title: Dengue: Seven more die as 1,753 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more people died of dengue, and 1,753 new patients were hospitalized across the country in 24 hours until 8am on Wednesday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 171 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, three were reported in Khulna division while one each in Chittagong, Mymensingh, Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions, it said.
Currently, 4,166 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at different hospitals across the country.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 56,916 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 52,579 have recovered.

item.title: West Bengal Muslims detained amid citizenship allegations
item.description:
At least nine Muslim men and two children have been detained in West Bengal since June over allegations that they are Bangladeshi nationals, with families claiming they were taken from their homes without being given adequate opportunity to establish their Indian citizenship, an investigation by Scroll has reported.
Most of those detained are from Murshidabad district, which shares a border with Bangladesh.
According to the investigation, several of the arrests took place during late-night raids. Relatives alleged that police personnel did not show arrest warrants, remand orders or copies of first information reports when taking the men away. In some cases, FIRs were reportedly filed weeks after the detentions.
The cases have emerged amid heightened scrutiny of alleged illegal migration from Bangladesh in West Bengal.
One of the cases concerns 61-year-old Ibrahim Sheikh of Ramakantapur village in Murshidabad.
Sheikh was taken from his home shortly after midnight on July 29, according to his daughter-in-law Parbin Khatun. She said several men in civilian clothes arrived at the house and asked Sheikh to produce identity documents.
After he showed his Aadhaar and voter cards, the men allegedly questioned whether he was Indian or Bangladeshi.
Khatun said Sheikh maintained that he was an Indian citizen, but the men claimed they had information suggesting otherwise and took him away.
The family subsequently approached the Suti police station with documents including pension records, land papers and Sheikh's voter card. They were not permitted to meet him and were later informed that he had been transferred to a detention centre.
The family says it has since been unable to determine his whereabouts.
At least four people among those detained had reportedly passed scrutiny during the Election Commission's recent special intensive revision of electoral rolls. Sheikh's appeal concerning his electoral status remains pending before an election tribunal, according to Scroll.
The investigation also found cases in which authorities allegedly attempted to deport detainees to Bangladesh.
In one case, 67-year-old Jalil Akhtar from Uttar Dinajpur district was detained on suspicion of being Bangladeshi. Police records cited by Scroll say he was subsequently handed over to the Border Security Force for deportation.
Akhtar reportedly maintained that he was an Indian citizen, after which the BSF returned him to police custody.
Police later registered a case against him under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, alleging that he was a foreign national who had entered India without valid travel documents.
His relatives produced land records dating back decades, while police questioned whether the documents established his relationship with his father.
The police inquiry also referred to Akhtar's inability to speak Bengali as one of the circumstances considered during the investigation. His family, however, speaks Surjapuri, a language used in parts of the Bihar-West Bengal border region and in Uttar Dinajpur's Islampur area.
Another case involves Abdul Jabbar of Murshidabad, who was detained along with his two sons, aged eight and six.
Jabbar's adoptive father told Scroll that police accused him of being Bangladeshi and initially asked the family to provide his documents.
The family says Jabbar possesses an Indian passport, voter card and other records. Police later produced a Bangladeshi birth certificate issued in 2022, which the family disputed.
Jabbar had also been included in the electoral rolls following the special intensive revision and had voted in the recent West Bengal Assembly elections, according to the report.
His wife, Jumman Bibi, said police later told her that Jabbar and the two children had been sent to Bangladesh. She said she last spoke to her husband on August 28 while he was being held at the Ahiran detention centre.
Another detainee, 28-year-old Sahin Sheikh, was taken from his home in Murshidabad's Budher Kismat village on June 14.
His wife said police accused him of being Bangladeshi despite his claim that he was born and had always lived in India. She said the family presented land records and a government-issued ration card, but police did not accept them.
A suo motu FIR was reportedly filed against Sheikh 20 days after his detention. According to his lawyer, the case relied partly on a photocopy of a Bangladeshi birth certificate found among his belongings, but the document had not been authenticated.
The lawyer has called for authorities to verify Sheikh's Indian voter card, school and panchayat certificates and land records.
Police officials have rejected allegations that the detentions were unlawful.
A senior officer at Suti police station said Ibrahim Sheikh's detention was carried out under a government executive order and that an FIR was not required.
Jangipur Superintendent of Police Surinder Singh said the authorities had acted according to government guidelines and claimed that Sheikh's family knew he was Bangladeshi.
Rights activists and lawyers have disputed the police position, arguing that people accused of being foreign nationals should be subjected to due legal procedures and given an opportunity to challenge the allegations.
Human rights activist Jakir Hussain said the practice of taking people into detention without producing them before a court raised serious legal concerns.
The detentions have also drawn attention because of remarks made in May by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who said suspected Bangladeshi infiltrators should be handed over directly to the BSF for deportation rather than being taken through court proceedings.
Adhikari also said that Hindu migrants eligible for citizenship under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, would not be targeted.
One detainee's family further alleged that police personnel made communal remarks during the detention, claiming that Hindus would receive preferential treatment compared with Muslims. The allegation could not be independently established by the report.
Several families are now pursuing legal remedies. Ibrahim Sheikh's family has approached the Calcutta High Court through a habeas corpus petition, while lawyers representing other detainees are also preparing or pursuing challenges to their detention.
The cases have raised questions over how citizenship claims are being assessed and whether detainees are being given sufficient legal opportunity to contest allegations that they are foreign nationals.

item.title: AIUB among Top 5 winners of University Innovation Exhibition Award
item.description:
The American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB) has been recognised as one of the top five winners of the University Innovation Exhibition Award at the Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026.
Organised by the Ministry of Science and Technology, the fair was held from September 12-14 at Novo Theatre in Dhaka under the theme “Innovate to Market.”
The event brought together universities, researchers, innovators, industry representatives, investors, policymakers, government officials, educators and students to promote innovation, entrepreneurship and the development of research and technological ideas into practical, market-oriented solutions.
The AIUB stall showcased various innovative projects and technological solutions and attracted visitors from government, industry, academia and research organisations.
Posts and Telecommunications, Information Technology and Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam, MP, and Science and Technology Secretary Md Anwar Hossain visited the AIUB stall and observed the projects and solutions showcased by the university.
More than 70 public and private universities from across Bangladesh participated in the fair, while five universities were selected for the University Innovation Exhibition Award.
AIUB credited its students, faculty members, researchers and participating teams for the achievement, and acknowledged the support of its relevant offices and management in promoting research, innovation and academic excellence.

item.title: Referees chief Webb 'really disappointed' over VAR error in Manchester derby
item.description:
Referees' chief Howard Webb said he was "really disappointed" with the VAR mistake that allowed Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby last weekend.
Haaland scored in the second half of City's victory against arch rivals United at Old Trafford on Sunday.
Haaland's close-range finish from Josko Gvardiol's cross was initially disallowed for offside, but VAR official Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus overturned the decision.
Donohue ruled City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play when he tried to reach the ball before it was finished off by Haaland.
City went on to win 1-0, but the result was overshadowed by the controversy involving the decisive goal.
United manager Michael Carrick said he was "staggered" by the decision because Fernandez blocked Lisandro Martinez's attempt to clear and potentially distracted goalkeeper Senne Lammens.
Donohue and Antrobus have been stood down by the Pro Ref organisation for this weekend's Premier League matches.
Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, said on the 'Match Officials: Mic'd Up' programme on Tuesday: "I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves.
"They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation.
"They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen."
Asked how the VAR officials had come to the conclusion that Fernandez was not interfering with play, Webb said: "In that moment, he (Donohue) gets tunnel vision.
"He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion.
"This goal should have been disallowed. We'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

item.title: Arteta salutes 'unbelievable' Dowman after Arsenal's teen star sinks Ipswich
item.description:
Mikel Arteta hailed the "unbelievable" Max Dowman after Arsenal's teenage sensation inspired their 4-2 win against Ipswich in the League Cup on Tuesday.
Arteta handed Dowman his first appearance this season and the 16-year-old seized his chance with two goals and an assist in the third round tie at Portman Road.
The Gunners boss once compared Dowman to Lionel Messi after the precocious playmaker burst onto the scene as a 15-year-old last season.
He played 13 times last season and became the youngest Premier League scorer ever against Everton in March.
But Arteta has been cautious in his use of Dowman, who has been an unused substitute several times this term.
Before the Ipswich game, Arteta said Dowman "will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else".
He has little need to hurry Dowman's development because Premier League champions Arsenal have so much experience and quality in their ranks.
However, even Arteta had to admit Dowman had delivered a masterclass against Ipswich.
"Unbelievable, he's unpredictable, he can go either way, so fluid, so nice to watch," the Spaniard said.
Dowman's previous appearance had come in the final game of last season against Crystal Palace, when Arsenal were already crowned champions.
He has since completed his GCSE exams and is looking forward to a bright future with Arsenal.
Dowman's potential is obvious but becoming a key player for Arsenal won't be easy.
Many teenage stars have flamed out before reaching their potential and Arteta is determined to be a nurturing presence for the youngster.
"He is 16, we don't really see that in the Premier League," Arteta said.
"In this environment, we want to develop him and we need to look after him."
With Dowman waiting in the wings, Arsenal will return to action at Brighton on Saturday in their last game before the international break.
Arteta's team have won all six of their matches this season across the Premier League, Champions League and League Cup.
Having made a host of changes against Ipswich, Arteta was impressed with the desire of his understudies.
"That's what we want to, to face every game, every competition with the same mentality, attitude and desire and so far we are doing it," he said.

item.title: NCC Bank holds 12th EGM

The 12th extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of National Credit and Commerce Bank PLC. (NCC Bank) was held on Tuesday, September 15, through a digital platform.
The meeting approved the proposed amendment to Article 108(1) of the Articles of Association of the Bank.
The meeting was presided over by chairman of NCC Bank Mohammed Nurun Newaz Salim, vice-chairman Abdus Salam, and among the directors, chairman of the executive committee Khairul Alam Chaklader; Md Moinuddin, Mohammed Sazzad Un Newaz; former vice-chairman Tanzina Ali; Syed Asif Nizamuddin; Shamima Newaz; Morshedul Alam Chaklader; Nahid Banu; and independent director Meer Sajed-Ul-Basher participated in the meeting through the digital platform.

In his remarks, managing director M Shamsul Arefin responded to various queries raised by the shareholders and a highlighted different aspect of NCC Bank’s continued progress and journey in the banking sector.

item.title: Bank Asia launches two-wheeler loan facility for customers
item.description:
Bank Asia PLC has launched a Two-Wheeler Loan facility to provide customers with easy and convenient financing for purchasing new two-wheelers.
Under this facility, customers will be able to purchase brand-new fuel-driven or electric two-wheelers for their personal, non-commercial use.
The new loan facility was inaugurated by ANM Mahfuz, additional managing director of the bank, on September 15, at a ceremony held at Bank Asia Tower, Karwan Bazar, Dhaka.
Zahed Chowdhury, head of asset, retail Banking, along with other senior officials of the bank, was also present at the event.
Under the two-wheeler loan facility, salaried individuals, self-employed professionals, businesspersons, individuals with regular and verifiable sources of income will be able to avail the loan facility ranging from a minimum of Tk50,000 to a maximum of Tk5 lakh at a competitive interest rate.
It will be up to 50% of the vehicle price. Customers will have the convenience of repaying the loan through Equal Monthly Installments (EMI) over a maximum tenure of four years.
Applicants must be at least 22 years of age, while the maximum age at loan maturity is 65 years.
Bank Asia continues to expand its retail banking services with a focus on providing need-based financial solutions that cater to the changing needs and lifestyles of its customers.
The newly launched loan product facilitates the customers to avail two-wheelers to meet their everyday transportation needs.

item.title: ONE Bank, BB sign agreement under Tk5,000cr CMSME refinance scheme
item.description:
ONE Bank PLC has signed a participation agreement with Bangladesh Bank under Bangladesh Bank’s Tk5,000 crore working capital refinance fund.
The initiative aims to disburse low-interest, soft-term working capital loans to the cottage, micro, small and medium enterprises (CMSME) and strengthen the sector.
The agreement was signed at Bangladesh Bank’s head office recently.
In presence of Md Anis Ur Rahman, deputy governor, Bangladesh Bank, the agreement was signed by Md Zabdul Islam, director, SME & Special Programs Department, Bangladesh Bank, and Kazi Ziaul Islam, deputy managing director and head of financial services and public sector, ONE Bank PLC, on behalf of their respective organizations.
The ceremony was also attended by Nahid Rahman, executive director; Shahahnaj Pervin, additional director, Bangladesh Bank, and Newaz Khalid Ahmed, senior executive vice president & head of commercial and SME business, ONE Bank PLC.
This working capital refinancing scheme is under Bangladesh Bank's Tk60,000 crore stimulus framework, and expected to facilitate shortfall under the CMSME business segment with better access to finance and lower rate of interest.
Through this refinancing scheme, ONE Bank will further strengthen its financing portfolio and will ensure support to the growth of CMSME in Bangladesh.
The scheme is designed to boost production capacity, create jobs and accelerate economic growth.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Efforts to continue until convicts brought back from India
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Wednesday said Bangladesh will take all necessary legal and diplomatic steps under existing laws to bring back convicted fugitives including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and those sentenced to death in the latest verdict.
She said the foreign ministry would initiate the required process with the Indian government once it officially receives all necessary documents related to the verdict delivered on Tuesday.
“Look, this is an ongoing process. I should not and do not wish to comment on the legal aspects,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Tuesday sentenced seven people including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader to death for their roles in suppressing the July 2024 mass uprising through incitement, provocation, attacks and killings.
Regarding the foreign ministry's responsibility, Shama said, “We are taking and will continue to take all necessary steps under existing laws to extradite convicted criminals, including the former prime minister of the fascist government and those sentenced yesterday (Tuesday).”
She said efforts are underway under the extradition treaty to bring back the former home minister, the former prime minister and the killers of martyr Hadi, who are currently detained in India. “Official correspondence is being exchanged,” she said.
“Since the verdict was delivered just yesterday (Tuesday), once we officially receive all the necessary paperwork, we will contact the Indian government through due process to take whatever steps are required,” said the state minister.
The government will certainly take all legal measures needed to bring the accused back to face justice, she added.
Asked whether Bangladesh has received any response from India to its earlier letter seeking the extradition of former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Shama said diplomatic communication is ongoing. “We have not yet received a definitive answer from India,” she said.
“However, from what we understand, they may have their own internal legal procedures to follow, and they are carrying out that process. These efforts will continue until we successfully bring them back to Bangladeshi soil,” she added.
Indian media outlet The Print claimed that India has not yet given its approval to Bangladesh for the appointment of Asad Alam Siam as Dhaka’s next high commissioner at New Delhi though the process to appoint new high commissioners and ambassadors by Dhaka for various foreign postings began in July.
Asked about media reports in Bangladesh and India, Shama urged the media not to publish such reports without official confirmation.
“I would request everyone not to pay heed to or publish such news reports until an official statement or concrete information is issued by either the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Government of India,” she said.
On an inter-ministerial meeting held on Tuesday regarding Bangladeshis travelling abroad with forged documents and false information, the state minister said the government is working to streamline the migration process for the large number of Bangladeshis living abroad.
“Ever since the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) formed the government, we have been working on how to streamline and consolidate the migration process for the vast number of Bangladeshi citizens living abroad,” she said.
The state minister noted that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had already taken several initiatives, including opening a dedicated Migration Wing.

item.title: Mahdi Amin: Bangladesh now a stable nation for investment
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Adviser and Prime Minister’s Office spokesperson Mahdi Amin has said Bangladesh has gained global recognition as a stable destination for investment.
He also said the government’s assurances on gas pressure to representatives of the business community and media are already showing results, with gas pressure increasing.
Mahdi Amin made the remarks at a special press conference at the Korobi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon on Wednesday afternoon.
He said inflation was also showing a positive trend, while prices of essential commodities had declined. He also claimed that diesel prices in Bangladesh were lower than in many other countries.
Highlighting what he described as government achievements, Mahdi Amin said technical education had been made mandatory up to Class VI.
He said initiatives had also been taken to establish a public university in Cox’s Bazar dedicated to research on the blue economy.
He said rooftop gardening programs had been introduced at educational institutions across the country.
Mahdi Amin also said pay scales ranging from Tk20,000 to Tk156,000 had been introduced for government financial benefits, and that legislation on property inheritance had been enacted.
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibli, Additional Press Secretary Atiqur Rahman Rumon and other relevant officials were present at the press conference.

item.title: Teacher killed in snatching: Motorcycle used in incident recovered, 2 arrested
item.description:
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DB) has arrested two more people in connection with the death of headmistress Ronjina Parveen, 55, who fell from a rickshaw after being pulled by snatchers in front of the South Plaza of the National Parliament House.
Police also recovered the motorcycle allegedly used in the snatching and Ronjina’s handbag.
Md Shafiqul Islam, additional police commissioner of the DB, confirmed the arrests and recoveries on Wednesday.
He said Ronjina’s handbag, along with a bus ticket found inside it, had been recovered. He said further details would be disclosed at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
Earlier, on August 30, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested Md Mosharraf Hossain Poni alias Poni Gazi and his associate Cedric in connection with the case.
At the time, RAB said it had recovered a Yamaha R15 motorcycle from them and claimed that it was the motorcycle used in the snatching.
Following the RAB briefing, however, Mosharraf told journalists that he was not involved in the incident. He also claimed that his motorcycle did not resemble the one used in the snatching.
CCTV footage recorded during the incident showed a blue motorcycle, while the motorcycle recovered by RAB was black and white, raising questions over whether it was the same vehicle.
The latest recovery is expected to clarify the discrepancy.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir stresses stronger global cooperation on health, SDGs
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Wednesday underscored the importance of international cooperation and multilateral partnerships in advancing health and achieving sustainable development goals.
He held a meeting with Dr Ahmed Jamsheed Mohamed, representative of the World Health Organization (WHO), at his office and discussed issues of mutual interest.
During the meeting, the state minister and the WHO Representative discussed matters of mutual interest, with particular emphasis on strengthening cooperation in the areas of public health, health security, disease prevention, and access to essential health services.
He appreciated the WHO’s continued cooperation and support in strengthening the country’s health sector and addressing emerging public health challenges.
The WHO Representative briefed the State Minister on the organization’s ongoing and planned cooperation in Bangladesh including support for health-system strengthening, capacity building, disease surveillance, and preparedness for public health emergencies.
Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening collaboration between Bangladesh and the WHO and agreed to continue close coordination on issues of common interest at national, regional, and international levels.

item.title: Complaint filed against 5 over alleged enforced disappearance, murder
item.description:
A formal complaint has been filed with the International Crimes Tribunal against five people, including former CTTC chief Asaduzzaman Miah and Additional Deputy Commissioner Ishtiaq Ahmed.
The complaint concerns the alleged enforced disappearance and murder of Abul Hossain Al Amin, principal of Ibn Masud Madrasa in Chattar, Gazipur.
Rashed Khan, political assistant to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, filed the complaint with the tribunal on Wednesday.
Earlier, the tribunal's investigation agency submitted its report to the prosecution, implicating five people, including then CTTC chief Asaduzzaman, ADC Ishtiaq Ahmed and then police inspector Asaduzzaman Miah.
According to sources familiar with the investigation, a group posing as Detective Branch (DB) police abducted Al Amin from Ibn Masud Madrasa in Gazipur on January 30, 2023. He has not been seen or heard from since.
The investigation report said Al Amin was tortured after being detained and allegedly died from the torture. His body was subsequently dumped in the Dhaleshwari River, according to the report.
The report said the CTTC unit arrested six people from different parts of the country on January 28, 2023. Based on information obtained during remand interrogations, a team led by then CTTC ADC Ishtiaq Ahmed detained Al Amin from the madrasa on January 30.
It was alleged that Al Amin was subjected to physical torture for 18 consecutive days at the CTTC office on Minto Road. He became critically ill and later died at the Central Police Hospital, according to the investigation report.
The report further alleged that the accused sought to conceal his death by dumping his body into the Dhaleshwari River from Tulsikhali Bridge in Keraniganj.

item.title: Teesta erosion leaves several hundred families homeless in northern districts
item.description:
At least 386 houses have been washed away by severe erosion along the Teesta River in five northern districts over the past seven days, leaving hundreds of families homeless.
The erosion has intensified at 113 points in Rangpur, Gaibandha, Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari and Kurigram, according to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).
Ahsan Habib, superintending engineer of the BWDB Rangpur regional office, said the situation has worsened rapidly in recent days.
“Erosion has intensified at 113 points in the five districts while 386 houses have been washed away in the past seven days,” he said.
He said there was insufficient allocation for erosion-control measures and the matter has been brought to the ministry’s attention.
In Gaibandha’s Sundarganj upazila, erosion has taken a particularly heavy toll on people living along the riverbank in Kapasia Union.
In Singijani and Bhorer Pakhi areas, residents said the river current increased suddenly, causing sections of the riverbank to collapse one after another.
Many families could not save their furniture, rice, clothes and other belongings as their houses collapsed.
Shahidul Islam, a resident of the area, said the erosion was so rapid that people barely had time to move their belongings to safety.
Ahad Mia said families are now facing an uncertain future after losing their homes and land.
Sundarganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer Iffat Jahan Tuli visited the affected areas and assured them of necessary assistance.
Gaibandha BWDB Executive Engineer Shariful Islam said geo-bags are being dumped at vulnerable points as an immediate measure.
“We are monitoring the situation and taking immediate preventive measures. Further steps will be taken based on the situation,” he said.
The erosion has also intensified in Kurigram’s Ulipur and Rajarhat upazilas, where around 80 houses have been washed away in the past week.
Families who have lost their homes are struggling to find safe places for themselves, their children and livestock.
In Lalmonirhat, all five upazilas have been affected by erosion.
BWDB Executive Engineer Sunil Roy said the intensity of erosion is increasing with fluctuations in the river’s water level.
Geo-textile materials have been placed at some vulnerable locations, he said but there was no allocation for permanent erosion-control work.
“As there is no allocation for permanent erosion-control work, there is little we can do beyond taking immediate measures,” he said.
Khuliagachh Union Parishad Chairman Khairuzzaman Badal said erosion is continuing almost every day.
In Rangpur, 53 houses have been washed away in Pirgachha, Kaunia and Gangachara upazilas during the past seven days, said BWDB Executive Engineer Hafiz Uddin.
The affected people said they needed permanent protection rather than temporary relief.
In Nilphamari, hundreds of erosion-hit families are spending their days in open spaces, on embankments or in relatives’ yards.
Many families have no arrangements for cooking and food, while residents said tents and dry food were urgently needed.
Abdul Karim of Char Kharibari said the river has eroded the area six times in two years.
“I have lost two houses to the river. Now I don’t know where to go,” he said.
Atwar Rahman said authorities often took measures only after houses began to collapse, rather than taking permanent steps to protect riverbank communities.

item.title: West Bengal IPS officer transferred after backlash over Islamic greetings
item.description:
A woman IPS officer in India’s West Bengal has been transferred after facing backlash from Hindu nationalist groups for using Islamic greetings such as “Assalamu Alaikum,” “Insha Allah” and “Jazakallah” in a video.
Bushra Bano, an Indian Police Service officer, was serving as additional superintendent of police (ASP) in Kharagpur before being transferred on Monday as deputy commandant of the State Armed Police (SAP), reports The Wire.
Bano had previously worked in Saudi Arabia before returning to India and clearing the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) examination twice.
The controversy began after a video featuring Bano’s use of Islamic phrases circulated on social media. Hindu nationalist accounts criticised her for not using slogans such as “Vande Mataram” or “Jai Hind.”
Controversial broadcaster Sudarshan News subsequently described the incident as “UPSC Jihad”, while an organisation called Hindu Legal Fund filed a complaint against Bano with West Bengal’s home secretary.
Bano was transferred a day after the complaint was filed.
The transfer has drawn criticism from opposition politicians and former bureaucrats.
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra criticised the move, contrasting it with India’s efforts to project a secular image at the recent BRICS summit.
Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi called for the IPS Association to intervene, alleging that Bano had been targeted by online trolling and criticising the state government for transferring her instead of supporting her.
Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi said Bano’s use of the phrases reflected her personal beliefs and did not undermine her commitment to serving the country.
He said pluralism in a diverse country like India was “not a weakness but a matter of pride.”

item.title: Rumon: Media must be more vigilant to prevent misinformation
item.description:
Additional Press Secretary to the Prime Minister Atikur Rahman Rumon has said misleading narratives are being created among the public through distorted and pieced-together news reports circulated across social media and other media platforms.
“Media outlets must perform their responsibilities with greater caution to prevent misinformation,” he said.
He made the comments at a special press conference held at the Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon on Wednesday.
Atikur Rahman said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has always believed in freedom of the media. However, he said media freedom must be accompanied by responsibility and caution in news reporting.
Citing examples of what he described as misinformation, Atikur Rahman said some individuals in a neighbouring country had distorted reports claiming that a temple had been demolished as part of new reform initiatives.
“In reality, the government is carrying out development work at the temple,” he said, adding that similar misinformation was also being spread by some individuals within Bangladesh.
Referring to the prime minister’s previous involvement with the newspaper industry, Atikur Rahman said: “Our prime minister was also associated with a newspaper. Just two days before becoming prime minister, he was the publisher of a newspaper. He believes in press freedom.”
Speaking about the government’s performance, the additional press secretary said only six months had passed since the government took office and that many initiatives would take time to produce visible results.
“Everyone needs to be patient to see the benefits of the government’s initiatives,” he said.
He said the prime minister had been working from morning until evening and that the country’s gas and electricity situation was now largely under control.
“The government is working to ensure comfort and peace in people’s lives. We have to work shoulder to shoulder to build a better Bangladesh,” he said.
Prime Minister’s Adviser and PMO spokesperson Mahdi Amin, Press Secretary Saleh Shibli, Deputy Press Secretaries Zahidul Islam Rony and Sujon Mahmud, and Assistant Press Secretary Nazmul Haque Khan were present at the press conference.
